# opal_access_rule (Data Source)

AccessRule DataSource

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "opal_access_rule" "my_accessrule" {
  id = "1b978423-db0a-4037-a4cf-f79c60cb67b3"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) The ID (group ID) of the access rule.

### Read-Only

- `admin_owner_id` (String) The ID of the owner of the group.
- `description` (String) A description of the group.
- `name` (String) The name of the access rule.
- `query` (String) JSON-encoded Opal Query body (OpalNodeQueryBody) defining the user set. Use `jsonencode({...})`. Provide at least one of `query` or `rule_clauses`; both AND. Omitting this attribute from configuration plans null and omits it on PUT, which clears that side on the REST API (optional-only so Terraform omit matches REST omit=clear).
- `rule_clauses` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rule_clauses))
- `status` (String) The status of the access rule.
- `uses_opal_query` (Boolean) True when the access rule stores an Opal Query (including hybrids). `query` is set when the REST dialect can express that filter; it is omitted for filters the API cannot express (e.g. risk, identity detection, agent fields). Rely on this flag, not only on whether `query` is present.

Read-Only:

### Nested Schema for `rule_clauses.unless.clauses.attribute_selectors`

Read-Only:

- `attribute` (String)
- `values` (List of String) Values to match; a user matches if their attribute equals any of them. For HR_IDP_STATUS, use HrIdpStatus values, or UNSET for users with no IDP status (shown as "Inactive"). UNSET must be the last value.
